sources.entry: VoxFlow - Open-source voice input workspace with local and cloud ASR, OCR, history, and coding-agent workflows. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/xingbofeng/VoxFlow) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: VoxFlow is an open-source voice input app for macOS, Windows, and iOS that inserts dictated text into any editable field and adds a local workbench for screenshots, recordings, clipboard items, and notes on macOS.
summary.what_it_does: Holding a dictation shortcut records speech and inserts the recognized text at the cursor in the current app, without submitting it. A keyboard launcher (⌥Space) searches recent local assets, runs actions, and can ask a configured LLM provider or open quicklinks to sites such as Google and GitHub. OCR runs on copied images (⌘⇧V) and on screen regions (⌘⇧A), with translation and summary options. Selected text can be translated, summarized, or sent to Task Assistant or Ask AI through explicit shortcuts. The app can also compose prompts for AI tools to paste manually, or dispatch spoken instructions to registered local coding-agent sessions such as Codex or Claude. It supports several ASR engines: Apple Speech by default, plus local models (e.g., Whisper, FunASR, Qwen3-ASR) and optional cloud providers (e.g., Groq) once configured.
use_cases: Dictate text into any app by voice
OCR text from screenshots or copied images
Search past dictations, screenshots, and clipboard history
Compose spoken prompts for ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor
Dispatch spoken tasks to local coding agents
Translate or summarize selected text by shortcut
how_to_run: Download VoxFlow-1.20.1-macOS.dmg from GitHub Releases and drag VoxFlow to Applications (macOS 15+)
Or download VoxFlow-1.20.1-windows-x64-setup.exe or the portable zip (Windows x64)
Grant Accessibility, Microphone, Speech Recognition, and Screen Recording permissions
Build from source: git clone the repository, cd VoxFlow, then run make run-dev
stack: Swift (macOS app, implied by macOS-specific permissions and Apple Speech)
Local ASR models: Qwen3-ASR, Whisper, FunASR, SenseVoice, Paraformer, NVIDIA Nemotron, Parakeet, Omnilingual, Confucius4-R2T2, FireRedASR2-AED, X-ASR-zh-en
Cloud ASR providers: Groq, Tencent Cloud, Alibaba Cloud
notable: Dictation inserts text at the cursor without stealing focus or auto-submitting
Local-first: history, assets, and non-secret settings stay on the Mac; cloud ASR and LLM calls are opt-in
Multiple speech engines, from built-in Apple Speech to local models and cloud providers
Local asset workbench making dictations, screenshots, recordings, clipboard items, and notes searchable
Local coding-agent dispatch limited to registered sessions
caveats: Workbench and local context features are described as macOS-only; Windows gets the dictation workflows
Some local models (Confucius4-R2T2, FireRedASR2-AED) need a separate download and at least 16 GB memory; R2T2 requires Apple Silicon
X-ASR-zh-en is still in acceptance testing and does not yet advertise file transcription
iOS IPA installation requires a device registered for this Ad Hoc release
